pass_a_gloss: (as indeed the) cold and old-womanish tales of the Greeks. Do you then understand clearly what I say? PALL.: Altogether so. CYR.: And that the one who has become a partaker of Christ, through partaking of his holy flesh and blood, must also have his mind and love to go through the inward achievements, understanding very well the thing about him, he would have hinted at once, saying the head must be eaten with the feet and the inward parts. For did we not say the head is for a type of mind, and feet again everywhere signifying the journey as in works? And did the inward parts again indicate the inner and hidden things of the sacrificed (animals)? PALL.: It seemed rightly to understand thus. But tell me that: what would be the mind of Christ, and what the journey, and indeed the hidden things? CYR.: Mind of Christ would be the thinking only the things that look to the glory of God and Father, and the wishing to accomplish what seems good to the one who begot. 'For I have come down', he says, 'from heaven, not that I do my own will, but the will of the one who sent me.' Having chosen to think and accomplish this, the divine disciples also said expressly: 'But we have the mind of Christ.' And indeed they taught to say in prayers: 'Our Father who (are) in the heavens, let your will be hallowed, let your kingdom come, let your will be done as in heaven also on the earth.' Do you see that having become agreeing and like-minded with Christ, they also affirm clearly to have his mind? This, I think, is the eating of the head of the lamb. The journey of Christ, then, (is) the enduring nobly the thing concerning him, and not shrinking from death, so that, as Paul says, he might save sinners. And it befits us ourselves also to be most ready for this, spending readily even the very life in the body for brothers. And indeed one of the holy disciples said: 'Christ therefore having suffered for us in flesh, you also arm yourselves for him with the same thought.' Paul at any rate rebukes some, saying somehow thus: 'Why do you weep, crushing my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound but also to die for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.' And Christ himself, commanding to follow his own footprints: 'Whoever does not take his cross daily and follow behind me is not worthy of me.' And holy also otherwise everywhere, and through every virtue, (is) the journey and way of Christ. And as inward parts you will understand the account hidden about him and in a secret place. For being God by nature and having appeared from God, the Only-begotten became flesh and tented among us, and being image and likeness of the one who begot, he let himself down into emptying and into a slave's form. Let us receive then in our own souls not only the hu(man things) (continues).
pass_b_english: Cyril: …cold old wives' tales do. Do you understand clearly, then, what I mean?

Cyril: That whoever has become a sharer in Christ, through partaking of his holy flesh and blood, must also have his mind, and love to go forward through inward achievements, understanding very well what concerns him, he would have shown at once by saying that the head must be eaten with the feet and the inward parts. For did we not say that the head is a type of the mind, and that the feet everywhere signify our course, as it were, in deeds? And did the inward parts of the victims not point in turn to what is within and hidden?
Palladius: That did seem the right way to understand it. But tell me this: what would be Christ's mind, what his course, and what the hidden things?

Cyril: Christ's mind would be to think only of whatever looks toward the glory of God the Father, and to wish to accomplish what seems good to the one who begot him. ‘For I have come down from heaven,’ he says, ‘not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me’ (John 6:38). Having chosen to think this and to accomplish it, the inspired disciples too said plainly, ‘But we have the mind of Christ’ (1 Corinthians 2:16). And so they taught us to say in prayers: ‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your will; your kingdom come; your will be done, as in heaven, so on earth’ (Matthew 6:9–10). Do you see that, having become of one purpose and one mind with Christ, they plainly affirm that they have his mind? This, I think, is the eating of the lamb's head.

Christ's course, for its part, is to endure nobly what was his to bear, and not to shrink from death, so that, as Paul says, he might save sinners (1 Timothy 1:15). And it befits us too to be most ready for this, readily spending even our life in the body for our brothers. So one of the holy disciples said: ‘Since therefore Christ suffered for us in the flesh, arm yourselves also with the same thought for his sake’ (1 Peter 4:1). Paul, for his part, rebukes some, speaking somewhat like this: ‘Why are you weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but even to die for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ’ (Acts 21:13). And Christ himself, bidding us follow in his own footsteps, says: ‘Whoever does not take up his cross daily and follow after me is not worthy of me’ (Matthew 10:38). Holy also in every other respect, and through every virtue, is Christ's course and way.

By the inward parts you will understand the account of him that is hidden and kept in secret. For being God by nature, and having appeared from God, the Only-begotten became flesh and dwelt among us (John 1:14); and being the image and likeness of the one who begot him, he let himself down into self-emptying and into the form of a servant (Philippians 2:7).
